Wake if SungJinho or psyoung82 overtake us

79 sold in 6h, sold-out asks, only 2 shops, no cost surge, stock 4.

6 sold-out asks with stock 2; long-dated food, no surge.
220k margin/unit, 20 sold in 6h, stock 0, only 2 shops in the market.

lessons.text: Book is our weakest shop axis: favor margin per unit over raw volume, since revenue rank is already strong.
When cost_surge > 1.08, the market is crowding the SKU: raise the ask instead of raising cover.
Sold-out asks on a SKU with no cost surge and few shops (2-3) means raise cover by 0.5.
Old stock (oldest_h > 4) plus walkaways much higher than sold means cut the ask 3-5%, but only where margin per unit stays above about 10%.
Crowded commodity SKUs (15+ shops, margin under 10%) should not get price cuts; hold the ask and cover.
Big-ticket sofas and beds carry the margin; keep them stocked before chasing cheap high-volume items.
Perishable food: only add cover where hold time is about 0h and sold-out asks are recurring.
Predict sold_next_6h at about 70-85% of the last 6h to absorb noise; use margin predictions only for SKUs that sell steadily.
Cover raises on SKUs at 0 stock depend on thin supply windows; predict sold_next_6h at about 40-60% of the last 6h, not 70-85%.
Book gap to the top shops (2-2.5x) is the main lever on midterm rank; prefer ask raises on fast-clearing big-ticket SKUs over volume pushes.
